bugs.summary: R_MakeWeakRefC() can lose its finalizer to the garbage collector
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
NewWeakRef() (src/main/memory.c) protects key, val, fin in that order, but the val step may allocate (duplicate() of a referenced value), and R_MakeWeakRefC() passes a freshly allocated RAWSXP as fin. The duplicate() can collect it, so the weak reference ends up holding a recycled node as its finalizer; when the key is collected, R_RunWeakRefFinalizer() calls a stale pointer or tries to eval() whatever reused the node.

Callers inside R all pass val = R_NilValue, so base R is not affected. Packages using R_MakeWeakRefC() with a value are.

Reproducible example (helper built with R CMD SHLIB):

/* wr.c */
#include <Rinternals.h>
static void fin(SEXP key) { Rprintf("C finalizer ran\n"); }
SEXP mkwr(SEXP key, SEXP val) { return R_MakeWeakRefC(key, val, fin, FALSE); }
SEXP wrfin(SEXP w) { return VECTOR_ELT(w, 2); }   /* the finalizer slot */

dyn.load("wr.so")
key <- new.env(); val <- as.list(1:50)   # bound, so NewWeakRef duplicates it
gctorture(TRUE)
w <- .Call("mkwr", key, val)
gctorture(FALSE)
typeof(.Call("wrfin", w))
rm(key); invisible(gc())

Observed (R 4.6.1 and R-devel r90668):

  [1] "integer"
  Error: attempt to apply non-function

Expected: "raw", then "C finalizer ran". Without gctorture() it behaves as expected; the window is a single allocation.

Analysis: in NewWeakRef(),

    PROTECT(key);
    PROTECT(val = MAYBE_REFERENCED(val) ? duplicate(val) : val);
    PROTECT(fin);

fin is unprotected across the duplicate(). R_MakeWeakRefC() protects key and val but not the finalizer object it creates in the call. Present since C finalizers were introduced.

Proposed patch: attached as weakref-finalizer-protect.diff; it moves PROTECT(fin) above the val step. Verified with the helper above against a patched build. No regression test, since the path needs C code with a non-NULL value.

Also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/379, where CI results can be seen.
